haiku-low.q1: A fallback: the 20-item popular list with fallback true, reason timeout (lookup over 30 ms) or no_features (no record).
haiku-low.q2: It keeps serving the records it has, up to 6 hours old. After that, records count as stale and requests fall back.
haiku-low.q3: No. Shadow output is never shown, and shadow runs after the response, so shadow failures cannot slow or break it.
haiku-low.q4: Users whose hash of salt plus user_id, mod 100, is below the shadow percent (10%); fallback responses are never shadowed.
haiku-low.q5: 7+ days in shadow, error rate under 0.5%, p99 under 80 ms, gate report under 24 hours old, ML lead approval, passing feature check.
haiku-low.q6: Not decided. Product has not chosen; the plan allows either a live A/B test or a direct switch to 100%.
haiku-low.q7: Each instance polls the registry every 10 seconds on a background thread, loads the new version there, then swaps its pointer atomically.
haiku-low.q8: Features come from the store record, copied as a snapshot into the shadow message. Shadow runs after the response, so adds no latency.
haiku-low.q9: A full buffer or unreachable queue drops the message and raises a counter, never blocking or retrying. High drops alert.
haiku-low.q10: Results store, keyed by request ID, holds both candidate and active items. The evaluation job compares overlap@20, rank correlation, empty lists and coverage.
haiku-low.q11: Shadow workers skip the model when a required feature is missing or the record is over 6 hours old; API falls back with missing_feature.
haiku-low.q12: One command swaps active and previous, with no approval. Both versions stay resident on every instance, so it takes effect within one 10-second poll.

sonnet.q1: A fallback response: the 20-item global popular list with fallback: true and reason timeout (lookup over 30 ms) or no_features (no record). The model is not called.
sonnet.q2: The store keeps serving the records it has. Requests use them until a record is older than 6 hours (now - materialized_at > 6h). After that the request falls back with reason stale. Alerts fire after 2 missed runs and a page at about 4 hours since the last success.
sonnet.q3: No. Shadow output is never shown and nothing on the request path reads it. Shadow runs after the response is written and in separate workers. A failure there, such as a full buffer, a queue outage or a worker crash, cannot slow or break the response. The message is dropped and counted.
sonnet.q4: 10% of users, chosen by bucket = hash(salt + user_id) mod 100 < percent, so a user is always in or always out. Only non-fallback requests, answered by the active model, are copied. Fallback requests are never shadowed.
sonnet.q5: All of these must hold. At least 7 days in shadow. Error rate under 0.5%. p99 inference latency under 80 ms. The latest gate report is no more than 24 hours old and meets those numbers. The ML lead has approved this exact version against a report no older than 24 hours. The feature check passes when re-run. If any fails, the promotion tool refuses and lists what is unmet.
sonnet.q6: Not decided. Product has not chosen whether a live A/B test comes between shadow and the full switch. The plan supports either option and builds neither.
sonnet.q7: Each instance polls the registry every 10 seconds on a background thread and caches the routing config in memory. If the active or previous version is not held, it loads that artifact in the background while requests keep using the current model. It swaps the in-memory pointer atomically only after the load succeeds. No redeploy is needed.
sonnet.q8: After responding, the API puts a message on a bounded, non-blocking in-process buffer. The message holds the request ID, user ID, the feature record snapshot the active model saw, the active version and the active output. A background thread ships the buffer to a message queue, and a separate shadow worker service consumes it and runs the candidate. The worker therefore uses the snapshot and does no second lookup. Shadow adds no latency because the response is written first, the enqueue never waits or retries on the request thread, and inference runs in separate workers.
sonnet.q9: A full API buffer or unreachable queue makes the message be dropped and a drop counter raised. Drops shrink the sample and are reported apart from candidate errors. A high drop rate raises an alert and the on-call may use the kill switch. There is no automatic disable. Messages also wait in the queue while a worker loads the candidate. Lost messages and worker crashes are counted as loss, not candidate errors. Workers scale and fail independently. Buffer and queue sizes are not set, because the request rate is unknown.
sonnet.q10: Shadow workers write one row per request to the results store, keyed by request ID. The row has candidate_items, active_items, candidate_latency, errors, skip reason, feature age, shadow_salt and versions. The hourly evaluation job counts only rows with the current salt and writes a gate report to the registry. The report holds error rate, p99 latency, days in shadow, skip and drop rates, and a comparison with the active model: overlap@20, rank correlation, share of empty or short lists, and catalogue coverage. It shows how different the candidate is, not whether it is better.
sonnet.q11: Several layers. Materialization writes the union of the features required by the active, previous and candidate versions. The promotion tool's feature check blocks starting shadow if a required feature is in no sampled record. The shadow worker checks each snapshot for every required feature and for age under 6 hours. If either fails it records a skip and does not run the model. This per-request check is the real guarantee. The API itself never runs the candidate. For the active model, a missing required feature gives a fallback.
sonnet.q12: One command swaps the fields: active = old previous, previous = old active. No approval is needed, and running it again rolls forward. It takes effect within 1 minute because instances poll every 10 seconds, plus the pointer swap time. Both active and previous models are already resident in memory on every instance, so no load is needed. Both versions' features stay in the materialization union. No redeploy is needed.
